The main problem with the game on the PS3 was how Sony set up the RAM. Sony decided to split the 512M of RAM into 256M for processing and 256 for video. Sort of like a current computer that has a video card. Where as Microsoft just dropped 512M of RAM into the console and made it available for anything.

So the developer, being lazy, built the game engine to just use the 512M of the Xbox and then tried to shoehorn it into the 256M of the PS3. Needless to say, that doesn't work and caused a lot of problems with the PS3 version.

Meanwhile companies like Naughty Dog learned how to use the dual memory system of the PS3 and made amazing games like Uncharted 3.

Now the PS4 memory and the Xbox 1 have pretty much the same memory layout, so you won't see anywhere near these kinds of problems in the future.

tl;dr - the developer didn't know how to code for the memory in the PS3, but the PS4 doesn't have that same problem.

I've backed 60. Yea, I know, I'm ~~addicted~~ hooked [or is that still too much for you /u/Medwynd]. The first thing you have to remember is that you probably are going to pay actually more than retail. With the advent of websites like miniaturemarket and even Amazon cutting their prices, you are going to pay more. So why do it? The main reason I do it is for exclusives and 'freebies' you get through the campaign. Unfortunately you probably won't know what the whole package is until the last couple of days, so I mostly just mark one that looks interesting and then when I get the notice there are 48 hours left I do my final research.

What I look for in a campaign? First, the game has to excite me as something new. If it is something I already have on the shelf, then I will typically pass. Second, it HAS to have a copy of the rules for me to download and check over. I always look over the rules to get a rough idea about the game. Third, I really look for a game play video. I typically will not back something that doesn't show what the game play is like. Finally, I really like a 3rd party review. Now, I know most of theses are paid, but I don't care. I like to see another set of eyes go over the game and give their opinion.

Okay, so the game has passed these test, what else. I never back a project from someone that is doing their first KS unless the campaign has been really well done. The biggest pain in the ass projects I've had have always been guys that have a great idea but don't know what they are doing. I really check over the 'freebies'. If they aren't worth the extra cost of the pledge, then I'll pass and buy retail. Finally, I like to look over their responses to the comments. If they can't handle a little constructive criticism, then I might pass.

Finally, there are some guys like CMON that just get a pass on most of this and I pledge right away. I am totally addicted to their mini's and have found most of their games to be fun if a little shallow.

On a side note, don't get hung up with when you are going to get your pledge. I bet 95% of pledges don't meet their goals. Almost always it is something to do with shipping or problems with the manufacturer. Those aren't going to go away. There is always going to be problems dealing with this but those problems would have been their for the retail release anyways. Anyone that didn't back the KS is going to have to wait those extra 6-8 months also, so when someone complains about how long a KS is taking I just sort of laugh at them.

On that note, there is a limit. If it takes years like almost every computer game I have backed then yea, bitching is fine. I won't ever back another computer game. They take foreffingever and it is so annoying.

P.S. I've only had 1 of those 60 games bail on the campaign. Fortunately for me, another company came in and completed the KS for free and I still got my game. I didn't get the sweet metal miniatures I paid for, but at least I got what I think is a pretty cool game. Now, I did have 1 problem where I guy got in over his head and couldn't pay the postage and I ended up sending him the postage to get the game, but that problem has been mostly solved with pretty much everyone charging S/H after the campaign. I also have a couple of computer games I've been waiting on for some time. Neither has been dumped, but that is one of the reasons I don't do computer game KS.
